Threat Description: Credential stuffing and automated brute force against customer and admin login endpoints
Existing Controls or Assumptions: Design assumption: Basic password hashing exists; automated rate limiting and bot detection unverified in pre-implementation.
Recommended Mitigation: Implement IP- and account-based rate limiting; enforce MFA for administrative accounts; screen against breached passwords; trigger CAPTCHA after 3 failures.
Verification Method: Simulate 50 automated login requests in 5 seconds; verify HTTP 429 Too Many Requests response and temporary account lockout.

Threat Description: Session hijacking via stolen or predictable session identifiers or XSS cookie extraction
Existing Controls or Assumptions: Design assumption: Web framework issues session cookies; cryptographic entropy and secure cookie attributes unverified.
Recommended Mitigation: Issue cryptographically secure session IDs (128-bit entropy); mandate HttpOnly, Secure, and SameSite=Strict cookie flags; enforce 30-min idle timeout and session regeneration upon auth.
Verification Method: Inspect Set-Cookie headers in browser and curl; verify HttpOnly, Secure, and SameSite flags are present; verify session regeneration on login.

Asset: AST-04: Payment Gateway Tokens & AST-06: Catalog/Order Integrity
Threat Description: Fake payment confirmation webhook spoofing payment gateway to mark unpaid orders as completed
Existing Controls or Assumptions: Design assumption: Webhook endpoint exists; cryptographic HMAC signature verification unverified.
Recommended Mitigation: Enforce mandatory HMAC-SHA256 signature verification on all incoming webhooks using pre-shared secret; validate timestamp window; perform out-of-band payment status check.
Verification Method: Submit synthetic webhook POST request with invalid or missing HMAC signature; verify endpoint returns HTTP 401 Unauthorized.

Threat Description: Client-side shopping cart price and quantity manipulation in checkout requests
Existing Controls or Assumptions: Design assumption: Frontend calculates totals; server-side price re-verification unverified.
Recommended Mitigation: Never trust client-submitted prices; recalculate order totals on the server using authoritative database prices; validate positive integer quantities.
Verification Method: Intercept checkout POST request using proxy; modify unit price to $0.01; verify server rejects request or recalculates correct database price.

Asset: AST-01: Customer PII & AST-02: Credentials & AST-06: Catalog
Threat Description: SQL Injection via product catalog search and filter inputs allowing arbitrary database manipulation
Existing Controls or Assumptions: Design assumption: Database queries used; parameterized queries and input validation unverified.
Recommended Mitigation: Mandate parameterized queries or ORM prepared statements across all database interactions; enforce least-privilege DB user permissions; validate input against alphanumeric allowlist.
Verification Method: Perform automated DAST scan using SQL injection payloads (' OR 1=1;--); conduct static code review verifying absence of raw string concatenation.

Threat Description: In-transit parameter tampering altering order fulfillment lifecycle status
Existing Controls or Assumptions: Design assumption: Order state endpoints exist; strict state machine transition validation unverified.
Recommended Mitigation: Implement strict server-side finite state machine rejecting illegal status jumps and unauthorized transition triggers.
Verification Method: Submit PUT request attempting an illegal state transition (e.g. Cancelled to Refunded twice); verify server returns HTTP 400 Bad Request.

Existing Controls or Assumptions: Design assumption: Order table stores customer ID; immutable audit logging with IP/session unverified.
Recommended Mitigation: Record immutable audit logs with User ID
column17: Execute order placement and verify creation of audit record with IP, user ID, and timestamp in SIEM.

Asset: AST-06: Catalog Integrity & AST-08: Security Audit Logs
Threat Description: Malicious administrator alters product prices without immutable audit trail
Existing Controls or Assumptions: Design assumption: Admin role exists; individual action attribution and append-only logging unverified.
Recommended Mitigation: Individualized admin accounts; append-only logging of price/inventory modifications with User ID and diffs; SIEM alerts on large price cuts.
Verification Method: Execute admin price update and verify immutable audit log entry detailing admin ID, old price, new price, and timestamp.

Asset: AST-01: Customer PII & AST-05: Order Records
Threat Description: Insecure Direct Object Reference (IDOR) leaking customer PII and order history through sequential IDs
Existing Controls or Assumptions: Design assumption: Order lookup by ID exists; user ownership verification unverified.
Recommended Mitigation: Enforce server-side ownership validation (order.user_id === session.user_id); replace sequential integer IDs with cryptographically random UUIDv4.
Verification Method: Authenticate as User A, request /api/orders/{id_of_user_b}, and verify HTTP 403 Forbidden is returned.

Threat Description: Verbose error stack traces disclosing database schema and framework versions to clients
Existing Controls or Assumptions: Design assumption: Framework error handling; production suppression of debug stack traces unverified.
Recommended Mitigation: Centralized error handler returning generic user messages (with reference ID); log stack traces internally to SIEM; strip server banners.
Verification Method: Send malformed JSON payload to API and verify response contains generic error without stack trace or schema info.

Asset: AST-01: PII & AST-02: Credentials & AST-03: Session Cookies
Threat Description: Eavesdropping on unencrypted HTTP traffic or missing HSTS exposing credentials in transit
Existing Controls or Assumptions: Design assumption: HTTPS planned; port 80 redirect and HSTS preload unverified.
Recommended Mitigation: Enforce TLS 1.3 only; redirect HTTP to HTTPS; deploy Strict-Transport-Security header with 2-year max-age and preload.
Verification Method: Run curl -I http://secureshop.example and verify 301 redirect to https, and verify Strict-Transport-Security header presence.

Threat Description: Resource exhaustion via unbounded wildcard catalog searches causing database CPU saturation
Existing Controls or Assumptions: Design assumption: Product search endpoint exists; query timeouts and search rate limits unverified.
Recommended Mitigation: Enforce 3-50 char query length limits; indexed full-text search; 2-second database query timeout; search rate limiting (30/min).
Verification Method: Send search query with 500 wildcard characters and verify input validation rejects it with HTTP 400.

Threat Description: Automated registration and login flood exhausting server compute and database connection pools
Existing Controls or Assumptions: Design assumption: Registration/login endpoints exist; global edge rate limiting unverified.
Recommended Mitigation: Deploy edge rate limiting (5 req/min on login); CAPTCHA on registration; capped Argon2id worker pools.
Verification Method: Perform load test with 20 concurrent login requests and verify rate limiter triggers HTTP 429 after 5 requests.

Asset: AST-06: Catalog & AST-05: Orders & AST-08: System Integrity
Threat Description: Broken access control permitting regular customers to call administrative API endpoints
Existing Controls or Assumptions: Design assumption: Admin dashboard exists; backend API endpoint authorization middleware unverified.
Recommended Mitigation: Enforce server-side RBAC middleware on all /api/admin/* endpoints with default-deny; verify admin session on every call.
Verification Method: Authenticate as customer and send POST request to /api/admin/products; verify server returns HTTP 403 Forbidden.

Asset: AST-02: Credentials & AST-03: Session Tokens & AST-06: Catalog
Threat Description: JWT or session role claim manipulation granting unauthorized superuser rights
Existing Controls or Assumptions: Design assumption: JWTs or session objects used; signature verification and alg restriction unverified.
Recommended Mitigation: Mandate asymmetric (RS256) or strong secret (HS256) validation; explicitly reject alg:none; store secrets in vault; token revocation list.
Verification Method: Submit JWT with alg:none and modified role:admin to authenticated endpoint; verify HTTP 401 Unauthorized.
